page_texts.3:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#decision-summary]

## Decision Summary

**Adopt Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS as the enterprise standard UI component system** for all new React-based frontend development at Gainwell Technologies. This stack supersedes any team-level component library choices (Material UI, Chakra UI, Ant Design, etc.) for new work. When complex data grid or charting requirements exceed what TanStack Table provides, **Kendo UI for React** is the approved supplementary solution.

---
page_texts.5:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Gainwell Technologies delivers healthcare SaaS products across a portfolio of React-based micro-frontends. Without a standardized component system, teams independently adopted Material UI, Chakra UI, Ant Design, and custom component libraries. This resulted in:

- Inconsistent visual language across product modules presented to the same end-user
- Duplicated accessibility remediation effort when WCAG audits found issues in team-specific components
- Commercial licensing cost and upgrade risk for teams using fee-based grid or charting libraries
- Bundle size violations when multiple component library runtimes were loaded in the same Module Federation host

The CTO has requested formalization of the UI component system to establish a consistent, accessible, and cost-controlled frontend foundation.
page_texts.6:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Architecture guidance [GUID-APP-TEC-003](../../strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md) documents the detailed selection criteria and evaluation of available component systems. The enterprise micro-frontend architecture (ADR-APP-002) requires that federated remote modules stay within a ≤500KB gzipped bundle budget per module; component library selection must account for this constraint.
page_texts.7:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Without a recorded enterprise decision:

- Teams choose different component libraries, creating visual inconsistency across micro-frontend compositions
- WCAG 2.2 AA compliance is achieved (or not) inconsistently, depending on which library a team adopted
- Module bundle budgets are violated by teams importing full component library runtimes
- The organization has no ability to enforce a unified design token system (see GUID-APP-UI-001) on top of multiple competing theming approaches
page_texts.8:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#decision-drivers]

### Decision Drivers

- 🎯 **WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility from the component layer**: Radix UI provides fully accessible, headless primitives — keyboard navigation, ARIA, and focus management are correct by default
- 🎯 **Zero commercial licensing cost for standard UI**: Radix UI, Shadcn/UI, Tailwind CSS, and TanStack Table are all open-source MIT licensed
- 🎯 **Bundle budget compliance**: Shadcn/UI components are copied into the codebase (no runtime library import); tree-shaking is total
- 🎯 **Design token integration**: Tailwind CSS CSS variables align directly with the enterprise design token taxonomy (GUID-APP-UI-001)
- 🎯 **Team code ownership**: Shadcn/UI's copy-into-codebase model gives teams full control over component source without upstream breaking-change risk
- ⚠️ **Constraint**: Cannot introduce Angular Material, Vue component libraries, or any framework-coupled component system (must be React-only)
- ⚠️ **Constraint**: Commercial grid/chart licensing must be justified by verified requirements before adoption

---
page_texts.9:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#required-option]

## Required Option

**Option 1: Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS (+ TanStack Table; Kendo UI when requirements demand it)** ✅ **SELECTED**
page_texts.11:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#core-stack]

#### Core Stack

| Layer            | Technology          | Role                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primitives       | Radix UI            | Accessible, unstyled headless component primitives                    |
| Component layer  | Shadcn/UI           | Pre-built components using Radix UI + Tailwind CSS; copied into repo  |
| Styling          | Tailwind CSS v3+    | Utility-first CSS; design token CSS variables mapped to Tailwind config |
| Data grid        | TanStack Table v8   | Headless table/grid for standard tabular data                         |
| Complex grid     | Kendo UI for React  | Full-featured grid/chart when TanStack Table is insufficient          |
page_texts.12:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#shadcnui-component-model]

#### Shadcn/UI Component Model

Shadcn/UI components are **not installed as an npm dependency**. The `shadcn` CLI copies component source files directly into the repository under `src/components/ui/`. Teams own that code and can modify it for product-specific requirements while retaining the Radix UI accessibility foundation.

```bash
# Initialize Shadcn/UI in a new React application
npx shadcn@latest init

# Add an individual component
npx shadcn@latest add button
npx shadcn@latest add dialog
npx shadcn@latest add data-table
```
page_texts.14:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#tanstack-table-standard-data-grid]

#### TanStack Table (Standard Data Grid)

TanStack Table v8 is the default for all tabular data requirements. It is headless (no default rendering), which means teams compose it with Shadcn/UI Table components and Tailwind CSS utility classes, staying within the enterprise design system.
page_texts.15:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#kendo-ui-for-react-complex-grid--charts--conditional]

#### Kendo UI for React (Complex Grid / Charts — Conditional)

Kendo UI for React is the approved solution when verified requirements exceed TanStack Table's capabilities (e.g., server-side virtual scrolling over 100K+ rows, pivot grid, Excel-like cell editing). Adoption requires:

1. A documented requirement that TanStack Table cannot satisfy
2. Architecture review approval (consistent with the ADR-GOV-001 technology governance gate)
3. License provisioning through Gainwell's existing Kendo UI enterprise agreement

When Kendo is introduced into an existing Shadcn/UI application, only the specific grid or chart component is replaced. The surrounding Shadcn/UI + Tailwind CSS components remain unchanged.
page_texts.16:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#benefits]

### Benefits

✅ WCAG 2.2 AA compliance achieved at the component primitive layer (Radix UI)
✅ Zero licensing cost for standard UI patterns
✅ Components copied into codebase — total tree-shaking, no upstream breaking changes
✅ Tailwind CSS integrates directly with enterprise design tokens (GUID-APP-UI-001)
✅ TanStack Table covers standard data grid needs without a commercial license
✅ Consistent visual language enforced across all product micro-frontends
✅ Bundle budget compliance: no full library runtime import
page_texts.17:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#risks-and-mitigations]

### Risks and Mitigations

⚠️ **Risk**: Teams continue using existing Material UI or Chakra UI components rather than migrating
🛡️ **Mitigation**: New work must use the standard stack; migration of existing components is planned per PTN-APP-MFE-005; architecture review gate enforces the standard for greenfield modules

⚠️ **Risk**: Shadcn/UI copied components diverge from the upstream base over time
🛡️ **Mitigation**: Teams run `npx shadcn@latest diff` periodically to surface upstream improvements; divergence is acceptable and expected for product-specific needs

⚠️ **Risk**: Kendo UI adoption spreads beyond justified complex grid/chart use cases
🛡️ **Mitigation**: Kendo adoption requires architecture review approval; GUID-APP-TEC-003 defines the requirement threshold

---
page_texts.19:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#option-2-material-ui-mui-v5]

### Option 2: Material UI (MUI) v5+

**Description**: Standardize on Material UI as the enterprise component library.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Large ecosystem and community
- ✅ Comprehensive component set out of the box
- ✅ Strong TypeScript support

**Cons:**
- ❌ Material Design visual language does not align with Gainwell's healthcare product design system
- ❌ MUI's CSS-in-JS (Emotion) runtime adds ~40KB gzipped overhead per module — conflicts with bundle budget
- ❌ WCAG accessibility depends on MUI team's release cadence; teams cannot fix accessibility issues without forking
- ❌ Theme customization requires learning MUI's proprietary `sx` prop and `ThemeProvider` API rather than standard CSS

**Verdict**: ❌ **Rejected** — CSS-in-JS runtime overhead, visual language mismatch, and inability to directly fix accessibility issues

---
page_texts.20:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#option-3-chakra-ui-v3]

### Option 3: Chakra UI v3

**Description**: Standardize on Chakra UI as the enterprise component library.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Good accessibility defaults
- ✅ Developer-friendly component API

**Cons:**
- ❌ Chakra UI v3 also uses a CSS-in-JS runtime, adding bundle overhead
- ❌ Less comprehensive data display components than Shadcn/UI
- ❌ Theming uses Chakra's proprietary theme object rather than Tailwind CSS variables; incompatible with enterprise design token strategy
- ❌ Smaller community than MUI or Tailwind-based stacks

**Verdict**: ❌ **Rejected** — Theming incompatibility with design token strategy; CSS-in-JS runtime overhead

---
page_texts.21:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#option-4-ant-design]

### Option 4: Ant Design

**Description**: Standardize on Ant Design (antd) as the enterprise component library.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Very comprehensive component set, including data grids and charts
- ✅ Strong TypeScript support

**Cons:**
- ❌ Ant Design visual language (Chinese enterprise aesthetic) does not match Gainwell product design requirements
- ❌ Large bundle size — full antd import is ~500KB+ gzipped, immediately violating the per-module budget
- ❌ WCAG compliance gaps in complex components; accessibility is not a first-class design goal
- ❌ i18n and locale handling tied to Ant Design's internal system

**Verdict**: ❌ **Rejected** — Bundle size violation, accessibility gaps, visual language mismatch

---
page_texts.22:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#option-5-no-standardization--teams-choose-independently]

### Option 5: No Standardization — Teams Choose Independently

**Description**: Allow each delivery team to select their own component library without enterprise mandate.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Maximum team autonomy

**Cons:**
- ❌ Inconsistent visual language across micro-frontend compositions
- ❌ WCAG compliance is uneven and difficult to audit
- ❌ Multiple component library runtimes in a single Module Federation host exceed bundle budget
- ❌ Duplicated effort: each team remediates accessibility issues in their chosen library
- ❌ No unified design token / theming strategy is achievable

**Verdict**: ❌ **Rejected** — Does not address any of the identified problems; creates governance and compliance risk

---
page_texts.23:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#decision-outcome]

## Decision Outcome

**Selected Option**: **Option 1 — Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS, with TanStack Table (standard) and Kendo UI for React (complex grid/chart when justified)**
page_texts.24:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#justification]

### Justification

Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS is the only evaluated stack that simultaneously satisfies all decision drivers:

- Radix UI provides WCAG 2.2 AA compliance from the primitive layer without requiring teams to reimplement keyboard navigation and ARIA
- Shadcn/UI's copy-into-codebase model eliminates bundle overhead from a runtime library import
- Tailwind CSS aligns with the enterprise design token strategy (GUID-APP-UI-001)
- All components are MIT open-source, eliminating commercial licensing cost for standard UI
page_texts.26:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#positive-outcomes-]

#### Positive Outcomes ✅

- Consistent visual and behavioral language across all micro-frontend products
- WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility baseline without per-team remediation effort
- No commercial licensing cost for standard UI components
- Enterprise design token system (GUID-APP-UI-001) is implementable across all products
- Bundle budget compliance for all standard component usage
page_texts.27:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#negative-outcomes-]

#### Negative Outcomes ⚠️

- Teams with existing Material UI, Chakra UI, or Ant Design components must migrate on their product roadmap (PTN-APP-MFE-005 provides the migration pattern)
- Shadcn/UI's copy-into-codebase model requires teams to actively adopt upstream improvements (not automatic)
- Kendo UI licensing must be tracked; consumption grows as complex grid requirements increase
page_texts.28:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md#neutral-outcomes-ℹ]

#### Neutral Outcomes ℹ️

- This decision does not affect backend technology selections
- React Native / mobile component selection is a separate decision outside this ADR's scope
